iterations.theme: Katolički pogled na usvajanje umjetne inteligencije: rad, dostojanstvo, supsidijarnost i posljednja ljudska uloga

sections.subtitle: Panel na Ascent Summitu: koja je posljednja ljudska uloga?
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj Louis Kim otvara emisiju u podcast kabini na Ascent Summitu i predstavlja sugovornike
sections.content:
Epizoda podcasta **The Catholic Futurist** snimljena je uživo na **Ascent Summitu**, u podcast kabini FIO-a. Voditelj **Louis Kim** okupio je trojicu sugovornika koji umjetnu inteligenciju promatraju iz vrlo različitih kutova. **Matthew Harvey Sanders** svakodnevno radi s AI agentima svih velikih laboratorija. **Taylor Black** djeluje istodobno u velikoj tehnološkoj kompaniji i u katoličkom svijetu. **Vincent Higgins** vodi industrijsku tvrtku koja AI donosi radnicima na terenu.

Već uvodni isječci najavljuju ton razgovora. Sanders otvara etičku dilemu koja će se provlačiti kroz cijelu raspravu: smije li poslodavac zaposliti čovjeka da kontrolira rad AI modela ako zna da će ga za četiri mjeseca, kada izađe novi i znatno bolji model, morati otpustiti? Higgins upozorava da se u razvoju softvera više ne traži netko tko piše kod, nego netko tko „dirigira orkestrom”. Black citira Kevina Scotta, koji voli reći da su mnoge teške stvari postale trivijalne, i postavlja protupitanje: koje su nemoguće stvari postale tek teške?

Kim zatim postavlja pitanje koje će zaokružiti cijelu emisiju: **koja je posljednja ljudska uloga?**
sections.subtitle_en: Panel at the Ascent Summit: what is the last human role?
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host Louis Kim opens the show in the podcast booth at the Ascent Summit and introduces the interlocutors
sections.content_en:
The episode of **The Catholic Futurist** podcast was recorded live at the **Ascent Summit**, in the FIO podcast booth. Host **Louis Kim** gathered three interlocutors who view artificial intelligence from very different angles. **Matthew Harvey Sanders** works daily with AI agents from all the major laboratories. **Taylor Black** operates simultaneously in a big tech company and in the Catholic world. **Vincent Higgins** leads an industrial company that brings AI to workers in the field.

Already the opening clips set the tone of the conversation. Sanders opens an ethical dilemma that will run throughout the entire discussion: may an employer hire a human being to oversee the work of an AI model if he knows that in four months, when a new and significantly better model is released, he will have to lay him off? Higgins warns that in software development one no longer looks for someone who writes code, but for someone who „conducts the orchestra”. Black quotes Kevin Scott, who likes to say that many hard things have become trivial, and asks a counter-question: what impossible things have become merely hard?

Kim then poses the question that will round out the entire show: **what is the last human role?**

sections.subtitle: Samo 20 posto Amerikanaca s optimizmom gleda na AI
sections.screenshot_description: Matthew Harvey Sanders govori o podatku da je samo petina Amerikanaca optimistična prema AI-ju
sections.content:
Na voditeljevo pitanje što ih je u usvajanju umjetne inteligencije iznenadilo, bilo brzinom bilo sporošću, prvi odgovara **Matthew Harvey Sanders**. Brzina usvajanja na razini velikih poduzeća njega ne čudi. Tvrtke uspoređuje s prekooceanskim brodovima kojima treba vremena da promijene smjer, no smatra da sve redom shvaćaju kako je riječ o pitanju opstanka.

Iznenadilo ga je nešto drugo: koliko je uspješna, kako je naziva, **propaganda** koja je prosječne ljude uvjerila da je AI prijetnja njihovoj budućnosti kojoj se treba oduprijeti. Dio javnosti, kaže, odbija koristiti tehnologiju u uvjerenju da time usmjerava čovječanstvo u boljem smjeru. Navodi i nedavno objavljen podatak, uz napomenu da se takve brojke mijenjaju iz tjedna u tjedan: **samo 20 posto Amerikanaca optimistično gleda na smjer razvoja umjetne inteligencije.**

Sanders priznaje i vlastitu odgovornost. Ljudi iz industrije, kaže, loše su objasnili koliko tehnologija može pomoći u borbi protiv najvećih nevolja ljudskog postojanja, poput **bolesti i neznanja**. Upozorava i na geopolitičku dimenziju: **Kina će nastaviti usvajati AI**. Ako Zapad tehnologiju odbija iz straha za vlastitu budućnost, a istodobno se boji svijeta u kojem Kina dominira umjetnom inteligencijom, to će za Zapad postati egzistencijalni problem.
sections.subtitle_en: Only 20 percent of Americans look at AI with optimism
sections.screenshot_description_en: Matthew Harvey Sanders talks about the data that only a fifth of Americans are optimistic about AI
sections.content_en:
To the host's question about what surprised them in the adoption of artificial intelligence, whether by its speed or its slowness, **Matthew Harvey Sanders** is the first to respond. The speed of adoption at the level of large enterprises does not surprise him. He compares companies to ocean liners that take time to change direction, but he believes that all of them understand that this is a matter of survival.

Something else surprised him: how successful, as he calls it, the **propaganda** has been that convinced average people that AI is a threat to their future that must be resisted. Part of the public, he says, refuses to use the technology in the belief that by doing so they are directing humanity in a better direction. He also cites a recently published data point, noting that such figures change from week to week: **only 20 percent of Americans look optimistically at the direction of the development of artificial intelligence.**

Sanders also acknowledges his own responsibility. People from the industry, he says, did a poor job of explaining how much technology can help in the fight against the greatest afflictions of human existence, such as **disease and ignorance**. He also warns of the geopolitical dimension: **China will continue to adopt AI**. If the West rejects the technology out of fear for its own future, while simultaneously fearing a world in which China dominates artificial intelligence, that will become an existential problem for the West.

sections.subtitle: AI razotkriva što mislimo o čovjeku
sections.screenshot_description: Taylor Black objašnjava da AI na vidjelo izvlači pretpostavke o tome što znači biti čovjek
sections.content:
Louis Kim zatim se obraća **Tayloru Blacku**, koji jednom nogom stoji u velikoj tehnološkoj kompaniji, a drugom u katoličkom svijetu. Black izdvaja dva zapažanja.

Prvo, AI je **tehnologija koju je teško dobro usvojiti**. Jednostavne primjene su lake. Svatko ga je, kaže, upotrijebio za neku zabavnu sitnicu, primjerice za igru riječi za bratovo vjenčanje. Sam ga je dan ranije koristio da izradi prikaz **svetog Ivana Zlatoustog s kriglom piva** za župni domjenak. Mnogo je zahtjevnije AI uklopiti u stvarne radne procese tako da i dalje dobro surađujete s drugim ljudima i da ne prepustite stroju kognitivne sposobnosti koje će vam kasnije trebati. Zato je usvajanje, kaže, vrlo neujednačeno, kako kod pojedinaca tako i u malim, srednjim i velikim tvrtkama.

Velika poduzeća imaju prednost jer su im podaci, procesi i poslovanje već strogo uređeni, pa AI uglavnom uvode u okruženju usklađenom s propisima. Za velik broj malih i srednjih poduzeća to ne vrijedi.

Drugo zapažanje je filozofsko. Usvajanje AI-ja **na vidjelo izvlači pretpostavke ljudi o tome što znači biti čovjek**. Rasprava o tome je li AI čovjek, smatra Black, srećom je završena, jer su to posve različite stvari. No onaj tko ima **siromašnu antropologiju** doista će zaključiti da AI može raditi sve što radi čovjek, ako misli da se čovjek svodi upravo na te radnje. Upravo zato, kaže, nova tehnologija otvara zanimljive razgovore do kojih inače ne bi došlo.
sections.subtitle_en: AI reveals what we think about the human being
sections.screenshot_description_en: Taylor Black explains that AI brings to light assumptions about what it means to be human
sections.content_en:
Louis Kim then turns to **Taylor Black**, who stands with one foot in a large tech company and the other in the Catholic world. Black singles out two observations.

First, AI is a **technology that is difficult to adopt well**. Simple applications are easy. Everyone, he says, has used it for some fun little thing, for example for a pun for a brother's wedding. He himself had used it the day before to create a depiction of **Saint John Chrysostom with a beer mug** for a parish reception. It is much more demanding to fit AI into real work processes in such a way that you still collaborate well with other people and do not surrender to the machine cognitive abilities that you will need later. That is why adoption, he says, is very uneven, both among individuals and in small, medium, and large companies.

Large enterprises have an advantage because their data, processes, and operations are already strictly regulated, so they mostly introduce AI in an environment aligned with regulations. For a large number of small and medium enterprises, that does not hold true.

The second observation is philosophical. The adoption of AI **brings to light people's assumptions about what it means to be human**. The debate about whether AI is human, Black believes, is fortunately over, because those are completely different things. But whoever has a **poor anthropology** will indeed conclude that AI can do everything a human does, if they think that a human is reduced precisely to those actions. That is precisely why, he says, the new technology opens up interesting conversations that would otherwise not take place.

sections.subtitle: Procesni dug i oprez radnika s ključem u ruci
sections.screenshot_description: Vincent Higgins objašnjava kako industrijski radnici na terenu provjeravaju svaki odgovor AI-ja
sections.content:
Voditelj zatim prenosi razgovor s partnerima konzultantske kuće **Bain**. Oni su mu rekli da je usvajanje sporije od očekivanog jer se zaboravlja koliko ljudskog rada postoji izvan ekrana, tipkovnice i miša. U organizacijama se nakupio **procesni dug**. Kim to ilustrira njihovom usporedbom: ako gradska vozila hitne pomoći zamijenite Ferrarijima, neće zbog toga brže prolaziti kroz semafore i zavoje.

Pitanje upućuje **Vincentu Higginsu**, direktoru industrijske tvrtke koja nije čisto AI kompanija, ali koristi umjetnu inteligenciju. Higgins objašnjava da njihov sustav donosi AI **industrijskom radniku na terenu**: radnik u mobilnom uređaju može razgovarati s AI-jem i dobiti uputu kako popraviti pumpu ili kako glasi sigurnosna procedura.

Tu, kaže, leži problem. **Ako AI odgovori pogrešno, posljedice mogu biti teške.** Zato je usvajanje sporije od očekivanog: na početku korisnici prate svako pitanje i svaki odgovor, a povjerenje grade postupno, kako vide učinke na terenu. Higgins naglašava da AI **nikada neće zamijeniti radnika s ključem u ruci**. Može mu pomoći, povećati sigurnost, poboljšati poslovanje i pouzdanost. Proces traje dulje jer inženjerski način razmišljanja traži kontrolu nad ishodima.
sections.subtitle_en: Process debt and the caution of the worker with a wrench in hand
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vincent Higgins explains how industrial field workers verify every AI answer
sections.content_en:
The host then conveys a conversation with partners from the consulting firm **Bain**. They told him that adoption is slower than expected because it is forgotten how much human labor exists beyond the screen, keyboard, and mouse. In organizations, **process debt** has accumulated. Kim illustrates this with their comparison: if you replace city ambulances with Ferraris, they will not pass through traffic lights and turns any faster because of it.

He directs the question to **Vincent Higgins**, director of an industrial company that is not purely an AI company, but uses artificial intelligence. Higgins explains that their system brings AI to the **industrial field worker**: on a mobile device, the worker can talk to the AI and receive instruction on how to repair a pump or what the safety procedure is.

There, he says, lies the problem. **If the AI answers incorrectly, the consequences can be severe.** That is why adoption is slower than expected: at the beginning, users monitor every question and every answer, and build trust gradually, as they see the effects in the field. Higgins emphasizes that AI **will never replace the worker with a wrench in hand**. It can help him, increase safety, improve operations, and reliability. The process takes longer because the engineering mindset demands control over outcomes.

sections.subtitle: Kontrola kvalitete i dilema: zaposliti nekoga na četiri mjeseca?
sections.screenshot_description: Matthew Harvey Sanders opisuje etičku dilemu zapošljavanja ljudi za kontrolu rada AI modela
sections.content:
Kim prenosi još jedno zapažanje iz Baina. Generativni AI nije deterministički, čak ni AI inženjeri ne razumiju sasvim što se događa unutar te crne kutije, pa je dio ušteđenog rada pojela **kontrola kvalitete (QA/QC)**. Čovjek i dalje mora biti uključen u proces. Kim zato pita kako se promijenio profil ljudi koje tvrtke zapošljavaju, primjerice na mjestima direktora informatike ili IT menadžera.

**Matthew Harvey Sanders** slaže se da je kontrola kvalitete trenutačno nužna, ali upozorava da se stvari mijenjaju iznimno brzo. Kao prijelomnu točku navodi studeni, kada je izašao model **Opus 4.5**. Taj datum smatra početkom doba AI-ja i robotike. Za zaposlenje u **Anthropicu**, objašnjava, treba položiti iznimno težak dvosatni test, a Opus 4.5 bio je prvi model koji ga je riješio bolje od ikojeg čovjeka u povijesti tvrtke.

Sanders priznaje da je programiranje specifično područje u koje se ulaže mnogo truda, ali vidi da se modeli počinju **generalizirati**. Model Astra opisuje kao „uznemirujuće općenit”, iako ga ne bi nazvao AGI-jem kao Jensen. Svako novo izdanje, kaže, u nečemu je bolje, a on sam sve manje vremena troši na kontrolu kvalitete.

To izravno utječe na zapošljavanje. Ako zaposli nekoga da provjerava rad modela, a za četiri mjeseca nova generacija bude, kako kaže, ne deset, ali možda pet puta bolja, što onda s tom osobom? **Je li ispravno zaposliti nekoga ako unaprijed zna da će ga za četiri mjeseca otpustiti?** Možda je bolje, razmišlja, da se sam nekako probije kroz posao, jer to ne želi učiniti ljudskoj osobi. Priznaje da je čudno svakodnevno se hrvati s takvim pitanjima.
sections.subtitle_en: Quality control and the dilemma: hire someone for four months?
sections.screenshot_description_en: Matthew Harvey Sanders describes the ethical dilemma of hiring people to oversee the work of AI models
sections.content_en:
Kim conveys another observation from Bain. Generative AI is not deterministic, not even AI engineers fully understand what is happening inside that black box, so part of the saved labor has been eaten up by **quality control (QA/QC)**. A human still needs to be included in the process. Kim therefore asks how the profile of people companies hire has changed, for example in positions of chief information officer or IT manager.

**Matthew Harvey Sanders** agrees that quality control is currently necessary, but warns that things are changing extremely rapidly. As a turning point, he cites November, when the **Opus 4.5** model came out. He considers that date the beginning of the era of AI and robotics. To be hired at **Anthropic**, he explains, one must pass an extremely difficult two-hour test, and Opus 4.5 was the first model that solved it better than any human in the company's history.

Sanders admits that programming is a specific area into which a lot of effort is invested, but he sees that models are beginning to **generalize**. He describes the Astra model as "disturbingly general," although he would not call it AGI like Jensen. Each new release, he says, is better at something, and he himself spends less and less time on quality control.

This directly affects hiring. If he hires someone to check the model's work, and in four months the new generation is, as he says, not ten, but perhaps five times better, what then with that person? **Is it right to hire someone if one knows in advance that they will be laid off in four months?** Perhaps it is better, he reflects, to somehow push through the work himself, because he does not want to do that to a human person. He admits that it is strange to wrestle with such questions on a daily basis.

sections.subtitle: Plavi ovratnici grade infrastrukturu, a politika šuti
sections.screenshot_description: Matthew Harvey Sanders upozorava na zamrznuto zapošljavanje bijelih ovratnika i manjak političke rasprave
sections.content:
Sanders zatim širi perspektivu na tržište rada. Trenutačno se, kaže, čuje da AI ne remeti bitno tržište rada i da se zapošljava više. No pomniji pogled na statistiku pokazuje da se zapošljavaju uglavnom **plavi ovratnici koji grade AI infrastrukturu**, dok je zapošljavanje **bijelih ovratnika praktički zamrznuto**.

Ako se trend nastavi, modeli će postati vrhunski u uredskim poslovima. Kada **utjelovljeni AI i roboti** postanu dovoljno sposobni, Sanders pita, zar se isto neće dogoditi i plavim ovratnicima? Svatko tko danas razmišlja o zapošljavanju, smatra, mora to uzeti u obzir.

Vjeruje da će to postati sve veći problem za američku administraciju. Kako će ljudima jamčiti da će imati posao? I ako ga neće imati, kako će im jamčiti da neće izgubiti domove? Najviše ga brine **koliko se malo o tome razgovara** izvan kruga nekolicine šefova AI laboratorija. Nema ozbiljnih rasprava o javnim politikama, a političari gotovo šute.

Posljedica je, upozorava, da ljudi, svjesni da bi tehnologija mogla imati negativan učinak, umjesto o rješenjima i o tome kako zajedno proći kroz razdoblje promjena počinju razmišljati iz **straha i ljutnje**. Boji se da bi se to s vremenom moglo nakupiti i prerasti u nagli izljev bijesa, što bi se moglo izbjeći kad bi se kao nacija otvoreno razgovaralo o tome kako proći kroz to razdoblje.
sections.subtitle_en: Blue-collar workers build infrastructure, and politics is silent
sections.screenshot_description_en: Matthew Harvey Sanders warns of frozen white-collar hiring and a lack of political debate
sections.content_en:
Sanders then broadens the perspective to the labor market. Currently, he says, one hears that AI is not significantly disrupting the labor market and that more hiring is taking place. However, a closer look at the statistics shows that it is mainly **blue-collar workers building AI infrastructure** who are being hired, while hiring of **white-collar workers is practically frozen**.

If the trend continues, models will become top-tier at office jobs. When **embodied AI and robots** become capable enough, Sanders asks, will the same not happen to blue-collar workers as well? Anyone thinking about employment today, he believes, must take this into account.

He believes that this will become an increasingly larger problem for the American administration. How will they guarantee people that they will have a job? And if they will not have one, how will they guarantee them that they will not lose their homes? What worries him most is **how little this is discussed** outside the circle of a few AI lab heads. There are no serious discussions about public policies, and politicians are virtually silent.

The consequence is, he warns, that people, aware that technology could have a negative effect, instead of thinking about solutions and how to go through the period of change together, begin to think out of **fear and anger**. He fears that over time this could accumulate and grow into a sudden outburst of rage, which could be avoided if there were open discussion as a nation about how to go through that period.

sections.subtitle: Ne programer, nego dirigent orkestra
sections.screenshot_description: Vincent Higgins opisuje novi profil zaposlenika koji usmjerava AI agente
sections.content:
Louis Kim najavljuje da će se kasnije vratiti na katoličku temu supsidijarnosti i suverenog AI-ja, ali prvo pita **Vincenta Higginsa** kako se promijenio profil ljudi koje zapošljava.

Higgins odgovara da se na razvojnoj strani danas **zapošljava netko tko dirigira orkestrom, a ne netko tko piše kod**. To smatra samorazumljivim. Takva osoba mora biti više generalist i mora biti vrlo pametna da bi dobro koristila alate. Alati su dostupni svima, napominje, ali ih ne koriste svi učinkovito.

Kao primjer navodi vlastitog voditelja AI-ja, **veterana s 40 godina iskustva** u razvoju softvera. On danas zapravo orkestrira: pokreće AI agente i s malim timom obavlja posao velikog tima.
sections.subtitle_en: Not a programmer, but an orchestra conductor
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vincent Higgins describes the new employee profile directing AI agents
sections.content_en:
Louis Kim announces that he will return later to the Catholic theme of subsidiarity and sovereign AI, but first asks **Vincent Higgins** how the profile of people he hires has changed.

Higgins replies that on the development side today, **someone who conducts an orchestra is hired, not someone who writes code**. He considers this self-evident. Such a person must be more of a generalist and must be very smart to use the tools well. The tools are available to everyone, he notes, but not everyone uses them effectively.

As an example, he mentions his own head of AI, **a veteran with 40 years of experience** in software development. Today, he actually orchestrates: he runs AI agents and, with a small team, does the work of a large team.

sections.subtitle: Otpuštanje dostojno čovjeka: što kaže katolički socijalni nauk
sections.screenshot_description: Taylor Black govori o odgovornosti poslodavca prema radniku u vrijeme otpuštanja
sections.content:
Kim se nadovezuje na Blackovu tvrdnju da je pitanje je li AI čovjek već pomalo izlizano. Njega je razdoblje AI-ja natjeralo da preispita i **odnose među ljudima**. Ako kritiziramo AI jer narušava odnos stroja i čovjeka, kaže, ni odnosi među ljudima nisu savršeni. Posebno se to vidi kod **otpuštanja**. AI će promijeniti sastav zaposlenih i donosit će se teške odluke. Zato pita sugovornike koliko su ponosni na to kako su dosad otpuštali ljude i koliko je to bilo u skladu s **katoličkim socijalnim naukom**.

**Taylor Black** navodi nekoliko okvira za otpuštanja bez krivnje radnika i za prijelazno razdoblje:

- **Zadržavanje nije uvijek usluga.** Ako nekoga držite na radnom mjestu koje neće imati vrijednost na tržištu, činite mu lošu uslugu. Poslodavac može biti zahvalan što je osoba bila dio tvrtke, ali ona mora misliti na vlastitu karijeru.
- **Očuvanje tržišne vrijednosti radnika** zadaća je svakog poslodavca: radnik treba moći ostati konkurentan, po mogućnosti u poslu koji voli, i prehraniti obitelj.
- **Prekvalifikacija i preusmjeravanje.** Tko ima resursa, može ponuditi prekvalifikaciju ili preusmjeriti vještine radnika prema područjima u kojima nastaje novi posao.

Black dodaje i misao koju je, kaže, Sanders već naznačio. AI nije koristan samo za uštede, nego i za **rješavanje novih vrsta problema koji ranije nisu bili isplativi**. Zato poslodavce potiče da otvore prostor za inovacije i zapitaju se koje su ideje svojedobno odložili jer nisu išle, a koje bi sada mogle postati dobra poslovna linija ili rješenje za novu vrstu kupaca. Takvi su pomaci teži jer ne slijede ustaljeni način rada. Zaključuje citatom Kevina Scotta: **mnoge teške stvari postale su trivijalne, a pitanje je koje su nemoguće stvari postale tek teške.**
sections.subtitle_en: A layoff worthy of human dignity: what Catholic social teaching says
sections.screenshot_description_en: Taylor Black speaks about the employer's responsibility towards the worker at a time of layoffs
sections.content_en:
Kim builds upon Black's claim that the question of whether AI is human is already somewhat worn out. The era of AI has forced him to also reconsider **relations between people**. If we criticize AI because it disrupts the relationship between machine and human, he says, relations between people are not perfect either. This is especially evident in **layoffs**. AI will change the composition of employees and difficult decisions will be made. Therefore, he asks the interlocutors how proud they are of how they have laid off people so far and how much that was in accordance with **Catholic social teaching**.

**Taylor Black** cites several frameworks for no-fault layoffs and for the transition period:

- **Retention is not always a favor.** If you keep someone in a job that will have no value on the market, you are doing them a disservice. An employer can be grateful that the person was part of the company, but that person must think about their own career.
- **Preserving the market value of the worker** is the duty of every employer: the worker should be able to remain competitive, preferably in a job they love, and support their family.
- **Retraining and redirection.** Whoever has the resources can offer retraining or redirect workers' skills toward areas where new work is emerging.

Black also adds a thought that, he says, Sanders had already indicated. AI is not useful only for savings, but also for **solving new types of problems that previously were not profitable**. Therefore, he encourages employers to open up space for innovation and ask themselves which ideas they once set aside because they did not work, and which could now become a good business line or a solution for a new type of customer. Such shifts are harder because they do not follow an established way of working. He concludes with a quote by Kevin Scott: **many hard things have become trivial, and the question is which impossible things have become merely hard.**

sections.subtitle: Suvereni AI u svakom kućanstvu kao odgovor na centralizaciju
sections.screenshot_description: Matthew Harvey Sanders govori o Papinom upozorenju na koncentraciju moći i ideji kućnog suverenog AI-ja
sections.content:
Kim najavljuje završni krug pitanja među sudionicima i u šali upozorava Sandersa da bi ga mogao prekinuti ako se previše raspriča. Zatim postavlja pitanje: kakav je katolički pogled na činjenicu da je AI, zbog golemog potrebnog kapitala, **centraliziran u nekoliko velikih kompanija**?

**Matthew Harvey Sanders** odgovara da je Papa dao prilično jasan smjer. Upozorio je da sadašnja centralizacija vodi **koncentraciji moći**, u kojoj nekolicina ljudi donosi odluke koje se tiču cijelog čovječanstva. Sanders to vidi kao egzistencijalnu prijetnju slobodi i ljudskom djelovanju. Papa je, smatra, otišao onoliko daleko koliko je mogao. Povijest pokazuje da to nije dobro, a najgore bi bilo prepustiti se struji kao da je sve neizbježno.

Zanimljivo je da ni sami šefovi laboratorija, prema njegovu uvjerenju, to ne žele. Morali su prikupiti toliko novca da su postali ovisni o ekonomskim interesima i, kako kaže, žele se osloboditi dioničara. Kao primjer navodi **Demisa Hassabisa** i druge koji traže regulaciju. Tvrdi da dioničari to sigurno ne traže, nego da šefovi laboratorija to osobno smatraju nužnim jer imaju djecu i brinu o svijetu u kojem će ona odrastati.

Sandersov odgovor je **suvereni AI na razini kućanstva**. Iznosi niz praktičnih koraka:

- **Dostupna računalna snaga.** Laboratoriji je otkupljuju godinama unaprijed. Uređaj **DGX Spark** tvrtke **Nvidia** trebao je, kaže, stajati oko 3.500 dolara, a sada je oko sedam tisuća i cijena raste.
- **Pritisak na izabrane dužnosnike**, kako bi znali da građanima nije svejedno mogu li sami pokretati AI. Ne bi svako pitanje, osobito osjetljivo, smjelo završiti u velikom laboratoriju. Ljudi bi trebali imati pravo na vlastitu računalnu snagu, modele i energiju za njih kod kuće.
- **Mali modeli su dovoljni.** Prosječan mali model danas, u odgovarajućem okruženju, može riješiti **90 do 95 posto** pitanja i zadataka. Zašto onda plaćati laboratorij, pita, ako se kod kuće plaća samo struja?
- **Konkretan prijedlog politici.** Vlast bi mogla od **Jensena Huanga** iz Nvidije zatražiti da **20 posto računalne snage prodaje potrošačima**, a ne sve velikim laboratorijima. Sanders vjeruje da bi Huang, koji je prema njegovim riječima upravo kupio Hugging Face i ulaže u Poolside, takvu viziju podržao. Ne bi to, međutim, mogao sam predložiti dioničarima.

Takav model AI-ja Sanders smatra izrazito usklađenim s **načelom supsidijarnosti** i učenjem Crkve, kao način da se odupre centralizaciji.
sections.subtitle_en: Sovereign AI in Every Household as an Answer to Centralization
sections.screenshot_description_en: Matthew Harvey Sanders speaks about the Pope's warning regarding the concentration of power and the idea of home sovereign AI
sections.content_en:
Kim announces the final round of questions among the participants and jokingly warns Sanders that he might interrupt him if he speaks too long. Then he asks the question: what is the Catholic perspective on the fact that AI, due to the enormous capital required, is **centralized in a few large companies**?

**Matthew Harvey Sanders** responds that the Pope gave a fairly clear direction. He warned that the current centralization leads to a **concentration of power**, in which a few people make decisions that affect all of humanity. Sanders sees this as an existential threat to freedom and human agency. The Pope, he believes, went as far as he could. History shows that this is not good, and the worst thing would be to go with the flow as if everything were inevitable.

Interestingly, even the laboratory heads themselves, according to his conviction, do not want this. They had to raise so much money that they became dependent on economic interests and, as he says, they want to free themselves from shareholders. As an example, he cites **Demis Hassabis** and others who call for regulation. He claims that shareholders certainly do not ask for that, but rather that lab heads personally consider it necessary because they have children and care about the world in which they will grow up.

Sanders's answer is **sovereign AI at the household level**. He outlines a series of practical steps:

- **Accessible computing power.** Laboratories buy it up years in advance. The **DGX Spark** device by the company **Nvidia** was supposed to, he says, cost around 3,500 dollars, and now it is around seven thousand and the price is rising.
- **Pressure on elected officials**, so they know that citizens care whether they can run AI themselves. Not every question, especially a sensitive one, should end up in a large lab. People should have the right to their own computing power, models, and energy for them at home.
- **Small models are sufficient.** An average small model today, in an appropriate environment, can solve **90 to 95 percent** of questions and tasks. Why then pay a lab, he asks, if at home one only pays for electricity?
- **A concrete proposal to politics.** The government could ask **Jensen Huang** of Nvidia to **sell 20 percent of computing power to consumers**, and not everything to large laboratories. Sanders believes that Huang, who according to him has just bought Hugging Face and is investing in Poolside, would support such a vision. However, he would not be able to propose that to shareholders on his own.

Sanders considers such an AI model to be highly aligned with the **principle of subsidiarity** and the teaching of the Church, as a way to resist centralization.

sections.subtitle: Odluke što bliže ljudima i kineski recept protiv otpuštanja
sections.screenshot_description: Matthew Harvey Sanders objašnjava supsidijarnost i kritizira kineski model zabrane otpuštanja
sections.content:
Louis Kim izravno pita: „Ne vjerujete centralizaciji moći?” Sanders odgovara kratko: „Ne, nimalo.” Kim napominje da je takvo nepovjerenje duboko ukorijenjeno u katoličkoj intelektualnoj tradiciji i moli ga da slušateljima pojasni **supsidijarnost**.

Sanders objašnjava: ako se nešto može učiniti na nižoj razini, tamo bi se i trebalo učiniti, jer odluke trebaju biti **što bliže ljudima**. Što su udaljenije od ljudi, veća je vjerojatnost da će se stvari raspasti. To svi instinktivno znamo, kaže, i to je jedan od razloga zašto ne vjerujemo političarima. Kim dodaje da postoji ljudski grijeh te da su očevi utemeljitelji sustav uzajamnih provjera i ravnoteže vlasti gradili na grčkoj filozofiji i **Polibiju**, na transparentnosti i raspodjeli moći.

Sanders zatim spominje Kinu. Ako se nastavi kretati prema centralizaciji, upozorava, nekolicina ljudi imat će golem utjecaj na politički sustav zbog moći i bogatstva kojim raspolaže. **Kineski odgovor na krizu zapošljavanja** je, prema njegovim riječima, zabrana otpuštanja. Sanders ga ne smatra rješenjem: tjerati čovjeka da ostane na poslu koji vjerojatno ni ne voli ne znači ići naprijed.

Cilj bi, smatra, trebao biti drugačiji. Svatko bi trebao moći koristiti AI da ostvari svoje snove, otkrije tko je i ispuni svoju svrhu. **Oslobađanje ljudi od mukotrpnog rada** nije loše, ali treba osigurati da ih postojeći ekonomski sustav pritom ne uništi.
sections.subtitle_en: Decisions as close to the people as possible and the Chinese recipe against layoffs
sections.screenshot_description_en: Matthew Harvey Sanders explains subsidiarity and criticizes the Chinese model of banning layoffs
sections.content_en:
Louis Kim asks directly: "You don't trust the centralization of power?" Sanders replies briefly: "No, not at all." Kim notes that such distrust is deeply rooted in the Catholic intellectual tradition and asks him to clarify **subsidiarity** for the listeners.

Sanders explains: if something can be done at a lower level, it should be done there, because decisions should be **as close to the people as possible**. The further away they are from people, the more likely things are to fall apart. We all know this instinctively, he says, and that is one of the reasons why we do not trust politicians. Kim adds that human sin exists and that the founding fathers built the system of checks and balances on Greek philosophy and **Polybius**, on transparency and the distribution of power.

Sanders then mentions China. If it continues to move toward centralization, he warns, a handful of people will have immense influence over the political system due to the power and wealth at their disposal. **The Chinese response to the employment crisis** is, according to him, a ban on layoffs. Sanders does not consider it a solution: forcing a person to stay at a job they probably don't even like does not mean moving forward.

The goal, he believes, should be different. Everyone should be able to use AI to realize their dreams, discover who they are, and fulfill their purpose. **Freeing people from drudgery** is not a bad thing, but we must ensure that the existing economic system does not destroy them in the process.

sections.subtitle: Više slobodnog vremena ili još više posla?
sections.screenshot_description: Taylor Black razmišlja o tome što znači katolička tvrtka i zašto radimo 40 sati tjedno
sections.content:
U završnom krugu svaki sudionik postavlja pitanje nekom od ostalih. **Vincent Higgins** pita **Taylora Blacka** što će se dogoditi s viškom slobodnog vremena koje AI obećava. Hoće li ga ljudi provoditi s obiteljima ili će se dogoditi suprotno, pa će zbog optimizacije dobiti još više posla?

Black smatra da to ovisi o **naravi tvrtke**. Zato hvali konferencije poput Ascenta, koje govore o izgradnji tvrtke s katoličkim karakterom. Nedavno je, priča, sudjelovao na forumu na kojem se raspravljalo što znači biti katolička tvrtka. U strogom smislu, napominje, katolički može biti samo čovjek. No sam pojam otvara pitanja: zašto smo **proizvoljno odabrali radni tjedan od 40 sati**? Ima li direktor tvrtke vrjedniji posao od **roditelja koji ostaje kod kuće s djecom**? Black nije siguran da je tako u katoličkom pogledu na svijet.

Tehnološki potres katoličkim graditeljima pruža priliku da **iznova osmisle tvrtku i narav rada** i da vrijednosti tvrtke usklade sa svojom teologijom i filozofijom. Navodi primjere eksperimenata koji i dalje imaju ekonomskog smisla:

- **bonus od 5.000 dolara za sklapanje braka**,
- **slobodni svi zapovijedani blagdani**,
- i slične mjere koje unose katolički karakter.

Sve to ide protiv toga da se zatečeno stanje prihvati zdravo za gotovo, jer je ono, kaže, nastalo razumno, ali povijesno nasumično, kroz sukob mnogih interesa.
sections.subtitle_en: More free time or even more work?
sections.screenshot_description_en: Taylor Black reflects on what a Catholic company means and why we work 40 hours a week
sections.content_en:
In the final round, each participant asks a question to one of the others. **Vincent Higgins** asks **Taylor Black** what will happen to the surplus of free time that AI promises. Will people spend it with their families, or will the opposite happen, so that due to optimization they will get even more work?

Black believes that this depends on the **nature of the company**. That is why he praises conferences like Ascent, which speak about building a company with a Catholic character. Recently, he recounts, he participated in a forum where it was discussed what it means to be a Catholic company. In a strict sense, he notes, only a human being can be Catholic. Yet the very concept opens questions: why did we **arbitrarily choose a 40-hour work week**? Does a company director have a more valuable job than a **parent who stays at home with the children**? Black is not sure that this is so in the Catholic worldview.

The technological earthquake provides Catholic builders an opportunity to **reimagine the company and the nature of work** and to align the company's values with their theology and philosophy. He cites examples of experiments that still make economic sense:

- **a $5,000 bonus for entering into marriage**,
- **all holy days of obligation off**,
- and similar measures that introduce a Catholic character.

All of this goes against taking the status quo for granted, because it was created, he says, reasonably, but historically randomly, through the clash of many interests.

sections.subtitle: Fizički AI: modeli na rubu mreže i kamere u slušalicama
sections.screenshot_description: Vincent Higgins objašnjava edge computing i upozorava na privatnost uređaja koji snimaju svakodnevicu
sections.content:
**Taylor Black** zatim pita **Vincenta Higginsa**. Čudi ga što se tako malo govori o mogućnostima AI-ja u istraživanju i u izgrađenom fizičkom svijetu, pa traži da iz industrijske perspektive objasni što vidi.

Higgins objašnjava da je **fizički AI** umjetna inteligencija koja nas doseže u stvarnom svijetu, a ne samo na ekranu. Njegova tvrtka gradi **hardver za edge computing**: model ostaje lokalno na uređaju, pa se dio odluka donosi bez oblaka. Ako se izgubi internetska veza, AI je i dalje dostupan, što je ključno na terenu, gdje se veza često gubi.

No razvoj fizičkog AI-ja ima i tamniju stranu. Razvijaju se mikrofoni i kamere koji, kako kaže, na pomalo zastrašujući način bilježe sve više našeg svijeta. Vidio je dizajne **slušalica s ugrađenim kamerama** koje razumiju kontekst: kad uđete u trgovinu, znaju što birate i kod koje ste police. Time se otvara **pitanje privatnosti**. Kad fizički AI dotakne svaki trenutak dana, upozorava Higgins, nalazimo se na skliskom terenu koji moramo pažljivo pratiti.
sections.subtitle_en: Physical AI: models at the edge of the network and cameras in headphones
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vincent Higgins explains edge computing and warns about the privacy of devices that record everyday life
sections.content_en:
**Taylor Black** then asks **Vincent Higgins**. He is surprised that so little is said about the possibilities of AI in research and in the built physical world, so he asks him to explain what he sees from an industrial perspective.

Higgins explains that **physical AI** is artificial intelligence that reaches us in the real world, and not just on a screen. His company builds **hardware for edge computing**: the model remains locally on the device, so part of the decisions are made without the cloud. If the internet connection is lost, AI is still available, which is crucial in the field, where the connection is often lost.

However, the development of physical AI also has a darker side. Microphones and cameras are being developed that, as he says, in a somewhat frightening way record more and more of our world. He has seen designs of **headphones with built-in cameras** that understand context: when you enter a store, they know what you are choosing and which shelf you are at. This opens up **the question of privacy**. When physical AI touches every moment of the day, Higgins warns, we find ourselves on slippery ground that we must monitor carefully.

sections.subtitle: Robotski psi u naftnoj industriji, humanoidi u našim domovima
sections.screenshot_description: Vincent Higgins govori o robotskim psima u inspekcijama i dolasku humanoidnih robota u kućanstva
sections.content:
**Matthew Harvey Sanders** ima dva pitanja za Higginsa. Prvo se tiče velikih laboratorija. Kako se približavaju AGI-ju, njihovi su modeli sve općenitiji, a Sanders je bio iznenađen koliko je Astra sposobna kada je utjelovljena u robotici. Brine li Higginsa da će laboratoriji jednostavno ući u hardver i preuzeti i industrijske radnike? U čemu je onda konkurentska prednost tvrtki koje razvijaju uređaje i industrija s mnogo iskustva i podataka u odnosu na laboratorij poput **OpenAI-ja**?

Higgins odgovara primjerom iz **naftne i plinske industrije**, gdje **robotski psi** već zamjenjuju ljude u inspekcijama. Mogu raditi gotovo sve što i čovjek: fotografirati i skenirati, i to u opasnim zonama u kojima ljudi ne bi trebali biti. To smatra vrlo pozitivnim.

Drugačije je kada se ista tehnologija stavi u **humanoidnog robota u domu**, koji šeće psa i kuha obroke. Tu postoje sigurnosna pitanja. Higgins procjenjuje da to nije pitanje sljedećih dvadeset, nego **sljedećih pet godina**. Humanoidi će isprva biti skupi, ali ništa ih, smatra, ne sprječava da uskoro uđu u domove. Zato poziva na promišljenost. Robot je u biti **utjelovljeni AI**: napredni modeli ugrađeni u glavu robota. To što su **multimodalni** i izvorno razumiju video i zvuk čini ih vrlo učinkovitima u opažanju okoline i snalaženju u njoj.
sections.subtitle_en: Robot dogs in the oil industry, humanoids in our homes
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vincent Higgins speaks about robot dogs in inspections and the arrival of humanoid robots in households
sections.content_en:
**Matthew Harvey Sanders** has two questions for Higgins. The first concerns the large labs. As they approach AGI, their models are increasingly general, and Sanders was surprised at how capable Astra is when embodied in robotics. Does it worry Higgins that the labs will simply enter hardware and take over industrial workers as well? What then is the competitive advantage of companies developing devices and industries with a lot of experience and data compared to a lab like **OpenAI**?

Higgins responds with an example from the **oil and gas industry**, where **robot dogs** are already replacing people in inspections. They can do almost everything a human can: take photographs and scan, and do so in hazardous zones where people should not be. He considers this very positive.

It is different when the same technology is placed into a **humanoid robot in the home**, which walks the dog and cooks meals. There are safety questions there. Higgins estimates that this is not a question of the next twenty, but of the **next five years**. Humanoids will initially be expensive, but nothing, he believes, prevents them from entering homes soon. Therefore, he calls for thoughtfulness. A robot is essentially **embodied AI**: advanced models built into the robot's head. The fact that they are **multimodal** and natively understand video and sound makes them very effective at perceiving the environment and navigating within it.

sections.subtitle: Tko je vlasnik vaših zdravstvenih podataka?
sections.screenshot_description: Matthew Harvey Sanders upozorava da biometrijski podaci s pametnih satova završavaju kod velikih kompanija
sections.content:
Sandersovo drugo pitanje odnosi se na zdravlje. Iznenađuje ga, kaže, **koliko se malo AI razvija u području preventivne medicine**. Gotovo svi nose pametne satove i narukvice koji prate biometriju, ali ti podaci uglavnom odlaze velikim kompanijama koje proizvode uređaje poput **Fitbita** i **Apple Watcha**. I tu vidi kretanje prema **centralizaciji osobnih medicinskih podataka**, uz vrlo malo suverenosti pojedinca. Ne zna mnogo tvrtki koje pokušavaju ljudima dati veću kontrolu nad vlastitim podacima, a područjem i dalje dominiraju veliki tehnološki igrači. Spominje i sugovornikovo ranije iskustvo rada na osobnom AI-ju u HP-u i pita vidi li ikakve znakove nade.

Prema transkriptu, odgovara voditelj **Louis Kim**. Nada je, kaže, u skladu s onim što je Sanders opisao o **lokalnom AI-ju**. Obrada svih biometrijskih podataka i predviđanje ishoda već je unutar dosega današnje računalne snage. Ključno je pitanje **gdje se ti podaci pohranjuju**. Kim, koji prati zbivanja u zdravstvu, slaže se da u tom smjeru nije vidio mnogo pomaka. Sanders zaključuje pozivom slušateljima: tu leži velika prilika, pa neka se netko prihvati posla.
sections.screenshot_description_en: Matthew Harvey Sanders warns that biometric data from smartwatches ends up with big companies
sections.content_en:
Sanders's second question relates to health. It surprises him, he says, **how little AI is developing in the field of preventive medicine**. Almost everyone wears smartwatches and wristbands that track biometrics, but that data mostly goes to large companies that produce devices like **Fitbit** and **Apple Watch**. And here he sees movement toward the **centralization of personal medical data**, with very little sovereignty for the individual. He does not know of many companies that are trying to give people greater control over their own data, and the field continues to be dominated by big tech players. He also mentions the interlocutor's earlier experience working on personal AI at HP and asks if he sees any signs of hope.

According to the transcript, host **Louis Kim** responds. Hope is, he says, in line with what Sanders described about **local AI**. Processing all biometric data and predicting outcomes is already within reach of today's computing power. The key question is **where that data is stored**. Kim, who follows developments in healthcare, agrees that he has not seen much movement in that direction. Sanders concludes with an appeal to the listeners: here lies a great opportunity, so let someone get to work.

sections.subtitle: Posljednja ljudska uloga: od hospicija do „Aliena” i „Heata”
sections.screenshot_description: Louis Kim govori o radu u hospiciju i pitanju posljednje ljudske uloge u zdravstvu
sections.content:
Kim zatim dijeli temu koja mu je osobno najbliža. Napustio je korporativni svijet velike tehnologije kako bi radio u **hospicijskoj i palijativnoj skrbi**. Zaokuplja ga pitanje: ako AI postane bolji u dijagnostici i ako se gotovo sve u zdravstvu može bolje obaviti uz AI, **koja je posljednja ljudska uloga?** Iz ontoloških i teoloških razloga, kaže, možda ćete htjeti ljudskog kapelana, iako je čovjek mrzovoljniji i manje prisutan od robota-kapelana koji je savršeno pažljiv. To naziva vrlo dobrim katoličkim problemom.

Sanders se prisjeća prvog filma **„Alien”**. Dok je čudovište na brodu, kapetan pita računalo kakve su im šanse za preživljavanje, a stroj odgovara da nemaju nikakve. Ta poruka, hladna poput natpisa „napustite svaku nadu”, pojavljuje se na ekranu i lik je samo čita. Sanders zamišlja kako bi ista vijest djelovala da ju je izgovorio čovjek koji te gleda u oči i dijeli tvoju sudbinu. Tako razmišlja i o hospiciju. Nada se da liječnici koriste AI, jer je dijagnostika s njim bolja. No ne želi ležati u krevetu dok tablet pokraj njega ne zazvoni s viješću da su mu šanse pale s deset na nula. Volio bi da se čovjeku kaže: tu vijest moraš prenijeti ti.

Kim objašnjava da ga upravo zato privlače **književnost i film**: mogu prenijeti ljudsko suosjećanje u situacijama u kojima ono nema logike. Jedna od njegovih najdražih filmskih scena je završetak filma **„Heat”**. Pacinov lik u zračnoj luci ustrijeli De Nirova pljačkaša banaka. Dok De Niro umire, pruža ruku, a Pacino je prihvaća, u potpunoj tišini, iako su bili smrtni neprijatelji. To je, kaže Kim, potpuno nelogičan i duboko ljudski čin. Kako algoritam ili robot programirati da to učini? To je, zaključuje, **otajstvo**.
sections.subtitle_en: The Last Human Role: From Hospice to "Alien" and "Heat"
sections.screenshot_description_en: Louis Kim speaks about working in hospice and the question of the last human role in healthcare
sections.content_en:
Kim then shares the topic that is personally closest to him. He left the corporate world of big tech to work in **hospice and palliative care**. He is preoccupied with the question: if AI becomes better at diagnostics and if almost everything in healthcare can be done better with AI, **what is the last human role?** For ontological and theological reasons, he says, you might want a human chaplain, even though a human is grumpier and less present than a robot chaplain that is perfectly attentive. He calls this a very good Catholic problem.

Sanders recalls the first film **"Alien"**. While the monster is on the ship, the captain asks the computer what their chances of survival are, and the machine answers that they have none. That message, cold like the inscription "abandon all hope", appears on the screen and the character simply reads it. Sanders imagines how that same news would feel if spoken by a human who looks you in the eye and shares your fate. That is how he thinks about hospice as well. He hopes doctors use AI, because diagnostics is better with it. But he does not want to lie in bed while the tablet next to him chimes with the news that his chances have dropped from ten to zero. He would like a human to be told: you have to deliver this news.

Kim explains that this is precisely why **literature and film** attract him: they can convey human compassion in situations where it makes no logic. One of his favorite movie scenes is the ending of the film **"Heat"**. Pacino's character shoots De Niro's bank robber at the airport. As De Niro is dying, he reaches out his hand, and Pacino takes it, in complete silence, even though they were mortal enemies. That is, Kim says, a completely illogical and deeply human act. How do you program an algorithm or a robot to do that? That is, he concludes, a **mystery**.

sections.subtitle: Što je katolički AI? Četiri odgovora u jednoj rečenici
sections.screenshot_description: Sudionici panela redom daju jednorečenične definicije katoličkog AI-ja
sections.content:
Za kraj Louis Kim traži od svakog sudionika da u jednoj rečenici odgovori **što je katolički AI**.

- **Matthew Harvey Sanders** kaže da je pojam tek potrebno definirati. U njegovoj tvrtki katolički AI shvaćaju kao onaj koji i u odgovorima i u vlastitom unutarnjem razmatranju uvijek uzima u obzir **Učiteljstvo** i čini sve što može da bude što vjerniji.
- **Taylor Black** katolički AI opisuje kao **granicu koja se ne može dosegnuti**, a koja pomaže razumjeti što znači biti ljudska osoba u katoličkoj antropologiji.
- **Vincent Higgins** naglašava da je katolički AI **ljudski procvat i uzdizanje osobe**. Ako AI koristimo ispravno, unutar katoličke vjere, bit ćemo bolji ljudi i procvast ćemo u svijetu.
- **Louis Kim** zaključuje da je **ljudsko dostojanstvo** u srži pristupa životu općenito, a tehnologija je **pojačalo i naših najboljih i naših najgorih strana**. Katolička je tradicija, kaže, dovoljno široka da o tome promišlja.

Kim zahvaljuje sugovornicima i zatvara epizodu podcasta The Catholic Futurist.
sections.subtitle_en: What is Catholic AI? Four answers in one sentence
sections.screenshot_description_en: Panel participants take turns giving one-sentence definitions of Catholic AI
sections.content_en:
In conclusion, Louis Kim asks each participant to answer in one sentence **what Catholic AI is**.

- **Matthew Harvey Sanders** says that the term has yet to be defined. In his company, they understand Catholic AI as one that, both in its answers and in its own internal deliberation, always takes into account the **Magisterium** and does everything it can to be as faithful as possible.
- **Taylor Black** describes Catholic AI as **a boundary that cannot be reached**, which helps understand what it means to be a human person in Catholic anthropology.
- **Vincent Higgins** emphasizes that Catholic AI is **human flourishing and the elevation of the person**. If we use AI correctly, within the Catholic faith, we will be better people and we will flourish in the world.
- **Louis Kim** concludes that **human dignity** is at the core of the approach to life in general, and technology is **an amplifier of both our best and our worst sides**. The Catholic tradition, he says, is broad enough to reflect on this.

Kim thanks the interlocutors and closes the episode of The Catholic Futurist podcast.
